name: Old Kingdom of Egypt
description: The age of the pyramid builders, when pharaohs ruled a unified Egypt from Memphis.

name: Indus Valley Civilization (Mature Phase)
description: Planned cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro flourished with drainage, standard weights and an undeciphered script.

name: Construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza
description: Construction of the largest Egyptian pyramid as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu

name: Akkadian Empire
description: Founded by Sargon of Akkad, often called the first empire, uniting the city-states of Mesopotamia.

name: Shang Dynasty
description: The first Chinese dynasty with written records, known for bronze work and oracle-bone inscriptions.

name: New Kingdom of Egypt
description: Egypt's imperial age of Hatshepsut, Akhenaten, Tutankhamun and Ramesses II.

name: Zhou Dynasty
description: China's longest dynasty; its later years saw Confucius, Laozi and the Warring States.

name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
description: Founded by Cyrus the Great, the largest empire of its time, stretching from the Indus to Egypt and Greece.

name: Roman Republic
description: Rome governed by elected magistrates and the Senate, expanding across the Mediterranean.

name: Greco-Persian Wars
description: Series of conflicts between Greek city-states and the Persian Empire

name: Peloponnesian War
description: War between Athens and Sparta that reshaped ancient Greece

name: Conquests of Alexander the Great
description: Military campaigns that created one of the largest empires of the ancient world

name: Maurya Empire
description: Founded by Chandragupta Maurya; under Ashoka it covered most of the Indian subcontinent and spread Buddhism.

name: Punic Wars
description: Three wars between Rome and Carthage for control of the western Mediterranean

name: Construction of the Great Wall of China
description: Qin Dynasty unified and extended earlier walls into a massive defensive fortification

name: Han Dynasty
description: A golden age that gave the Chinese people their name, opened the Silk Road and invented paper.

name: Fall of the Roman Republic
description: Period of political upheaval leading to the end of the Roman Republic and rise of the Empire

name: Pax Romana
description: Period of relative peace and stability across the Roman Empire

name: Roman Empire
description: From Augustus to the fall of the West, Rome ruled the Mediterranean world and shaped European law, language and culture.

name: Classic Maya
description: City-states such as Tikal and Palenque flourished with monumental pyramids, writing and astronomy.

name: Gupta Empire
description: India's classical age of mathematics, astronomy, literature and art; the decimal system and zero took shape.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: The eastern Roman Empire, ruled from Constantinople, preserving Greek and Roman learning for a thousand years.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Decline and collapse of the western half of the Roman Empire

name: Tang Dynasty
description: A cosmopolitan golden age of Chinese poetry, trade and woodblock printing.

name: Umayyad Caliphate
description: The first hereditary Islamic dynasty, ruling from Damascus over lands from Spain to Central Asia.

name: Islamic Golden Age
description: Period of cultural, economic, and scientific flourishing in the Islamic world

name: Abbasid Caliphate
description: Ruled from Baghdad, home of the House of Wisdom and the Islamic Golden Age, until the Mongols sacked the city.

name: Viking Age
description: Period of Norse exploration, expansion, and raids across Europe

name: Holy Roman Empire
description: A union of central European territories, from Charlemagne's coronation until Napoleon dissolved it.

name: Chola Empire
description: A south Indian maritime empire whose navy reached Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia; builders of great temples.

name: Song Dynasty
description: An age of invention in China, with movable type, the compass, gunpowder weapons and paper money.

name: The Crusades
description: Series of religious wars sanctioned by the Latin Church to recover the Holy Land

name: Mongol Conquests
description: Rapid expansion of the Mongol Empire across Asia and Europe

name: Delhi Sultanate
description: A series of five dynasties ruling much of northern India from Delhi until the Mughal conquest.

name: Mali Empire
description: A West African empire grown rich on gold and salt trade; Timbuktu became a centre of learning.

name: Ottoman Empire
description: From Anatolia it grew to rule southeastern Europe, the Middle East and North Africa for six centuries.

name: Vijayanagara Empire
description: A south Indian empire centred on its capital at Hampi, a great Hindu power of the age.

name: The Black Death
description: Devastating pandemic of bubonic plague that killed an estimated one-third of Europe's population

name: Ming Dynasty
description: Built the Forbidden City and most of today's Great Wall; Zheng He's fleets sailed to Africa.

name: Italian Renaissance
description: Cultural movement that profoundly affected European intellectual life with advances in art, architecture, and science

name: Aztec Empire
description: A Mesoamerican empire ruled from Tenochtitlan, conquered by Hernán Cortés.

name: Inca Empire
description: The largest empire in the pre-Columbian Americas, linked by roads along the Andes; conquered by Pizarro.

name: Gutenberg's Printing Press
description: Development of movable-type printing in Europe, revolutionizing the spread of knowledge

name: Age of Exploration
description: European exploration and colonization of the Americas, Africa, and Asia

name: Safavid Empire
description: A Persian dynasty that made Shia Islam the state religion of Iran.

name: Protestant Reformation
description: Religious reform movement that led to the creation of Protestant churches

name: Mughal Empire
description: Islamic empire that ruled much of the Indian subcontinent

name: Scientific Revolution
description: Period of major advances in mathematics, physics, astronomy, and biology

name: Tokugawa Shogunate
description: Two and a half centuries of peace and isolation in Japan under military rulers, ended by the Meiji Restoration.

name: Construction of the Taj Mahal
description: Construction of the iconic marble mausoleum in Agra, India

name: English Civil War
description: Series of civil wars between Parliamentarians and Royalists over governance of England

name: Qing Dynasty
description: China's last imperial dynasty, founded by the Manchus and ended by the 1911 revolution.

name: Maratha Empire
description: Founded by Shivaji, it came to dominate much of India before falling to the British East India Company.

name: Glorious Revolution
description: Overthrow of King James II of England by William of Orange

name: Industrial Revolution
description: Transition from agrarian economies to industrial manufacturing in Britain and beyond

name: American Revolution
description: Colonial revolt that led to the independence of the United States

name: French Revolution
description: Political upheaval in France that overthrew the monarchy and established a republic

name: Haitian Revolution
description: Successful slave revolt that established Haiti as the first free black republic

name: Napoleonic Wars
description: Series of conflicts involving Napoleon's French Empire against European coalitions

name: Latin American Wars of Independence
description: Series of revolutions that freed most of Latin America from Spanish and Portuguese rule

name: Opium Wars
description: Conflicts between China and Western powers over trade and sovereignty

name: California Gold Rush
description: Mass migration to California after gold was discovered at Sutter's Mill

name: British Raj
description: Direct British Crown rule over the Indian subcontinent, from the 1857 rebellion until independence and partition.

name: American Civil War
description: War between the Union and Confederate states over slavery and states' rights

name: Meiji Restoration
description: Modernization of Japan under Emperor Meiji, transforming it into an industrial power

name: Scramble for Africa
description: Rapid colonization of the African continent by European powers

name: Construction of the Eiffel Tower
description: Building of the iconic iron lattice tower in Paris for the 1889 World's Fair

name: Boxer Rebellion
description: Anti-foreign uprising in China suppressed by an international coalition

name: Russo-Japanese War
description: Military conflict in which Japan defeated Russia, shifting power dynamics in East Asia

name: World War I
description: Global conflict centered in Europe involving the Allied and Central Powers

name: Russian Revolution
description: Revolution that overthrew the Russian monarchy and established the Soviet Union

name: Spanish Flu Pandemic
description: Deadly influenza pandemic that infected a third of the world's population

name: Indian Independence Movement
description: Movement led by Gandhi and others that achieved Indian independence from British rule

name: Soviet Union
description: The communist state formed after the Russian Revolution, a superpower of the Cold War until its dissolution.

name: Chinese Civil War
description: War between the Nationalists and Communists that established the People's Republic of China

name: The Great Depression
description: Severe worldwide economic downturn that began with the US stock market crash

name: Spanish Civil War
description: Civil war between Republicans and Nationalists led by Francisco Franco

name: World War II
description: Global conflict between the Allies and the Axis powers

name: The Holocaust
description: Systematic genocide of six million Jews by Nazi Germany

name: Manhattan Project
description: Secret research program that developed the first nuclear weapons

name: Korean War
description: War between North and South Korea involving international forces

name: Cuban Revolution
description: Armed revolt led by Fidel Castro that overthrew the Batista regime

name: American Civil Rights Movement
description: Movement to end racial segregation and discrimination in the United States

name: Vietnam War
description: Prolonged conflict between communist North Vietnam and US-backed South Vietnam

name: Space Race
description: Competition between the USA and USSR for spaceflight supremacy

name: Construction of the Sydney Opera House
description: Building of the iconic performing arts center in Sydney, Australia

name: Chinese Cultural Revolution
description: Sociopolitical movement launched by Mao Zedong to enforce communism

name: Watergate Scandal
description: Political scandal that led to the resignation of US President Richard Nixon

name: Iranian Revolution
description: Revolution that overthrew the Shah and established an Islamic republic

name: Soviet-Afghan War
description: Soviet military intervention in Afghanistan that became a prolonged guerrilla conflict

name: End of Apartheid
description: Dismantling of the apartheid system in South Africa, culminating in democratic elections

name: Human Genome Project
description: International research project to map all human genes

name: Bosnian War
description: Ethnic conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina following the breakup of Yugoslavia

name: Dot-com Bubble
description: Speculative bubble in internet-related companies that burst in 2000

name: War on Terror
description: Global military campaign against terrorist organizations following the September 11 attacks

name: Iraq War
description: US-led invasion and occupation of Iraq

name: Arab Spring
description: Wave of pro-democracy protests and uprisings across the Arab world

name: COVID-19 Pandemic
description: Global pandemic caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus
